kaps_punt: nie-lewende dinge kan nie al die sewe lewensprosesse uitvoer nie; sommige dinge het gelewe en is nou dood: dooie hout, droë blare

items.bewering: 'n Nie-lewende ding kan nie al sewe die lewensprosesse doen nie. Dit het nooit gelewe nie, en dit kan ook nie doodgaan nie.
items.bron: Seven life processes (movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion, nutrition; MRS GREN) as the criteria for living things: twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes; thescienceteacher.co.uk/mrs-gren. Something that never lived cannot die; it follows from 'dood' meaning it once lived. The three-way split (living / dead / never lived) is the lesson's design choice and was not tested.

items.bewering: 'n Lepel van metaal kry byvoorbeeld nie self kos nie en groei nooit nie.
items.bron: Nutrition means an organism takes in and uses food; growth means a lasting increase in size or mass (twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes). A metal spoon does neither.

items.bewering: Toets 'n muntstuk teen die sewe prosesse: hy kry nooit self kos nie. Hy voel niks van jou hand nie, en hy maak nooit nuwe muntstukke nie.
items.bron: South African coins are metal: plated steel, copper-nickel, aluminium-bronze (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coins_of_the_South_African_rand; en.numista.com/437972). Nutrition, sensitivity and reproduction as defined at twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes. A coin does none of them.

items.bewering: 'n Gewone klip uit die tuin kan self nie een van die sewe doen nie, dus lewe dit nie.
items.bron: Against the seven criteria (twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes): a stone moves only when something pushes it, and does not feed, grow, reproduce, respire, excrete or sense. 'self' makes the claim exact. The lesson does not put the stone through the two questions, so a limestone or shell-rich stone, which does come from living things, does not arise here.

items.bewering: 'n Motor beweeg, maar hy lewe nie. Die motor kry nie self kos nie, en hy maak nooit motortjies nie.
items.blok: Beweeg is nie dieselfde as lewe nie
items.bron: Reproduction means making new organisms of the same kind, and nutrition means the organism takes in food itself (twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes). A car is fuelled by people and never makes cars. That movement alone is the usual false test children use is documented by the Victorian Department of Education science continuum, 'Living things' (education.vic.gov.au, citing Skamp 2004 and Kyle et al. 1989).

items.bewering: 'n Rivier beweeg ook, maar hy kry nie self kos nie. Een of twee prosesse alleen is dus nog nie 'n bewys van lewe nie.
items.blok: Beweeg is nie dieselfde as lewe nie
items.bron: MRS GREN is used as a set: a thing must do all seven (thescienceteacher.co.uk/mrs-gren; twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes). On its own the sentence is true. Note for the writer, not a fact finding: the lesson later treats a single process as the evidence that the bean lives ('stoot hy 'n wortel uit... Die boontjie lewe dus nog'). That is sound only because the thing already comes from a living thing (see the item on the sorting rule), but read side by side the two blocks seem to say opposite things.

items.bewering: Vuur beweeg en lyk asof hy kos kry en groei, want hy verbrand hout en word groter.
items.blok: Vuur lyk lewend, maar lewe nie
items.bron: Western Fire Chiefs Association, 'Is Fire Alive?' (wfca.com, 27 Feb 2024): fire consumes fuel to sustain itself, and it grows as a result of the oxygen and fuel around it. The burning-as-eating comparison is held at 'lyk asof', so the mapping does not teach that fire really eats; it holds.

items.bewering: Tog lewe vuur nie, want hy merk niks op van wat om hom gebeur nie en reageer nie self daarop nie.
items.blok: Vuur lyk lewend, maar lewe nie
items.bron: WFCA, 'Is Fire Alive?' (wfca.com, 2024): sensitivity / response to stimuli is 'debated, but by a biological definition, no'; a fire that could respond would avoid firefighting foam. The strongest scientific reason is that fire is not made of cells (WFCA; straightdope.com 'Why don't we consider fire alive?'), but that lies outside the seven-process frame this lesson uses. Within that frame, sensitivity is a defensible reason for Grade 4, and 'self' covers fire flaring up when wind blows on it. The Victorian DET continuum notes that fire is a known hard case for this age.

items.bewering: So kan 'n ding selfs lyk asof dit 'n paar van die prosesse doen, en tog lewe dit nie.
items.blok: Vuur lyk lewend, maar lewe nie
items.bron: WFCA 'Is Fire Alive?'; straightdope.com: fire shows several functional traits of living things (metabolism, growth) and is still not alive.

items.bewering: Sommige dinge het vroeër gelewe, en hulle is nou dood. Dooie hout kom van 'n boom wat al sewe die lewensprosesse gedoen het.
items.blok: Dinge wat gelewe het en nou dood is
items.bron: Plants carry out all seven life processes, with movement and sensitivity shown through tropisms, sun-tracking and the like (thescienceteacher.co.uk 'Seven life processes and plants' PDF; tutorchase.com 'How do plants demonstrate the seven life processes?').

items.bewering: 'n Tak breek af en droog uit, en dan is die tak dood.
items.blok: Dinge wat gelewe het en nou dood is
items.bron: Deadwood: 'a branch or a part of a tree that is dead' (vocabulary.com); 'dead branches or completely dead standing trees' (USDA NAL Thesaurus, lod.nal.usda.gov). The sentence rightly ties death to the drying out, not to the breaking off, so it stays true where a fresh cutting can still root.

items.bewering: Droë blare het ook eers aan 'n lewende plant gegroei en kos gemaak. Vandag kan daardie hout en daardie blare nie een van die sewe doen nie.
items.blok: Dinge wat gelewe het en nou dood is
items.bron: Leaves make the plant's food by photosynthesis. As a leaf dies the plant cuts off its supply, the chlorophyll goes first, and the leaf dries out and dies (I'm a Scientist Q&A 'why do leaves turn colours and die in autumn', archive.imascientist.org.uk). Dead woody biomass is 'non-living' (UN-REDD glossary 'dead wood').

items.bewering: Twee vrae help jou om te kies tussen dood en nie-lewend. Vra eers of die ding van iets kom wat gelewe het. Vra dan of dit nog self kos kry of kan groei. ... Die lepel van metaal en die muntstuk kom nie van iets wat gelewe het nie. Hulle het dus nooit gelewe nie en is nie-lewend. (with the list 'Sorteer met twee vrae')
items.bron: The rule was tested as a set on every example the lesson sorts. Metal spoon and coin: Q1 no, so never lived (metal; Wikipedia coins of the rand). Dry leaf: Q1 yes, Q2 no, so dead (imascientist). Dead wood: Q1 yes, Q2 no, so dead (USDA NAL; UN-REDD). Dry bean: Q1 yes, Q2 can grow, so alive (dry seeds are alive with suspended metabolism; pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6613187). Car and river: Q1 no, so never lived, consistent with block 3. Fire is routed by name to the seven-process test, so the rule never sorts it. Every example lands correctly. Two limits outside the lesson's own examples, reported for a person rather than as findings: Q1 read as 'made by a living thing' would put honey or an eggshell in 'dood'; and a learner may not be able to tell beforehand whether something 'only looks' as if it feeds or grows.

items.bewering: Die droë blaar kom van 'n plant, dus het hy gelewe. Vandag kry hy nie meer self kos nie en kan hy nie meer groei nie, dus is hy dood.
items.bron: A leaf is part of a living plant and dies when the plant cuts off its supply (archive.imascientist.org.uk). Dead leaf tissue does not photosynthesise or grow.

items.bewering: 'n Droë boontjie lyk net so droog soos 'n droë blaar.
items.bron: This compares appearance only, and the block's point is that appearance does not decide whether a thing lives, so the mapping holds. Dry seeds are desiccated but living (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6613187: the embryo becomes desiccation tolerant at maturity and stays so until germination).

items.bewering: Sit die boontjie in klam grond, dan stoot hy 'n wortel uit. Die boontjie lewe dus nog, maar die droë blaar is dood.
items.bron: Germination order: imbibition, then the radicle (first root) emerges, typically over several days to two weeks (GRDC GrowNote Soybean, grdc.com.au; UW Extension Soybean Growth and Development guide). But not every dry bean sprouts. Seed viability declines with age and storage: soybean lots stored 3, 19 and 22 years showed about 2%, 40% and 99% mortality (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8869448), and 'after physiological maturity the viability of seed gradually declines' (FUNAAB PCP 504 lecture). Taken literally, the sentence promises that every dry bean will grow a root. A learner who plants an old or damaged bean sees that promise fail, and may conclude that dry beans are not alive. The conclusion, that a dry bean is a living seed, is right. The unconditional promise is not.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier and keep the claim. Say that a dry bean put in damp soil USUALLY pushes out a root after a few days, and that this shows it is still alive. Do not cut the evidence, and do not claim every bean will sprout. The list item 'Kan dit nog? Dan lewe dit, soos 'n droë boontjie' can stay as it is once this block is narrowed.

items.bewering: Iets wat net lyk asof dit kos kry of groei, soos vuur, toets jy teen al sewe die lewensprosesse en nie met die twee vrae nie.
items.bron: This is a procedure, not a fact. Its premise, that fire only appears to feed and grow, matches WFCA 'Is Fire Alive?' (2024) and the Victorian DET 'Living things' continuum, which treats fire as the hard case. See the sorting-rule item for its limit.

items.bewering: lewensprosesse: Die sewe dinge wat saam wys dat iets lewe.
items.bron: Read alone. There are seven life processes, and they work as a set (MRS GREN: twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes; thescienceteacher.co.uk/mrs-gren). 'saam' correctly says they are judged together.

items.bewering: nie-lewend: 'n Ding wat nooit gelewe het nie en nie kan lewe nie.
items.bron: Read alone. It is consistent with the lesson's three-way convention, which the brief exempts, and true of every example the lesson puts in this class (spoon, coin, car, river, stone).

items.bewering: dood: Iets wat vroeër gelewe het, maar nou nie een van die lewensprosesse meer kan doen nie.
items.bron: Read alone. It fits dead wood and leaves: 'non-living woody biomass' (UN-REDD glossary); a dead leaf no longer photosynthesises or grows (imascientist). It does not wrongly take in the dormant bean, which can still grow.

items.bewering: dooie hout: Hout van 'n boom of 'n tak wat nie meer lewe nie.
items.bron: Read alone. It matches 'a branch or a part of a tree that is dead' (vocabulary.com) and 'dead branches or completely dead standing trees' (USDA NAL Thesaurus). It is true whichever noun 'wat nie meer lewe nie' attaches to.

items.bewering: 'n Rivier se water beweeg afdraand. (implied: a river is not alive)
items.bron: River water flows downhill under gravity, and a river does not feed or reproduce (seven-process criteria, twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes). Children counting moving water as alive is a documented misconception (Victorian DET 'Living things' continuum).

items.bewering: 'n Droë blaar en 'n muntstuk lê in die tuin. Watter een het gelewe ... (implied: the leaf lived, the coin did not)
items.bron: As for the items on the dry leaf and the coin above (imascientist; Wikipedia coins of the rand).

items.bewering: 'n Hond en 'n motor beweeg albei. Noem drie prosesse wat net die hond kan doen. (implied: at least three processes only the dog does)
items.bron: A car does not grow, reproduce or feed itself. Respiration, excretion and sensitivity are also absent in the biological sense, though exhaust and sensors invite argument (twinkl.com/teaching-wiki/seven-life-processes). At least three clean answers exist (growth, reproduction, nutrition), so the question's premise holds.

opsomming: One claim is contradicted and goes back to the writer: the bean block promises that every dry bean in damp soil pushes out a root, but stored seed loses viability, so it should say a bean usually sprouts after a few days; everything else holds, including the two-question sort on all of the lesson's own examples, both comparisons, and the reason given for fire, and the lesson contains no superlatives.
